subject: SLA terms for Quantara deployment - uptime & monthly credit structure
messages:
From: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@quantara.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@quantara.io
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA terms for Quantara deployment — uptime and credits

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the throughput improvements on batched inference. Before we proceed to SOW sign, Quantara needs the hosting SLA to reflect our regulated production needs. High level asks:

- Baseline uptime of 99.99% (we run mission-critical user flows)
- Monthly service credits that are meaningful and uncapped for sustained downtime (we'd like the standard % credit applied per incident, with no low monthly cap)
- Explicit latency commitments for user-facing endpoints (p95 < 200ms ideally)

Can you share Redwood's standard SLA template and whether you can accommodate tighter uptime/credit mechanics? We can be flexible on price if you can meet the availability requirement. Attached our draft SOW for context.

Regards,
Tim
Tim Sullivan
Head of Infrastructure, Quantara
procurement@quantara.io

Attachment: Quantara_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@quantara.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA terms for Quantara deployment — uptime and credits

Hi Tim — great to hear the demo landed well. Appreciate the detail; sharing a quick read on how we typically structure availability and credits, and where we have flexibility.

Quick summary (Redwood standard template):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime for hosted API endpoints
- Remedy: tiered monthly credit bands tied to percent below uptime (e.g., 99.5-99.94 = 10% invoice credit; 99.0-99.49 = 25%; <99.0 = 50%), with a monthly cap at 40% of that month’s invoice
- Latency: we publish p95 guidance per model/route; we do not currently include hard latency credits on standard hosted plans but can evaluate for enterprise routes

Where we can be pragmatic for Quantara:
- For a committed Dedicated seat or Dedicated+Private routing, we can discuss an uplift to 99.97% or a localized regional SLA.
- On credits: instead of uncapped credits, we propose a higher trial cap for the ramp period — e.g., a 60% monthly cap for the first 3 months, stepping down to 40% thereafter.
- For latency: we can include an annex with a p95 target and a modest credit (one-time invoice credit) if the target is missed more than twice in a month for user-facing endpoints; batched workloads would have a separate tolerance.

I’ve looped in Ben (CS lead) to surface operational impact and Laura from legal will review redlines — cc'd Ben. If that approach sounds acceptable, I’ll ask legal to draft a short SLA annex and we can iterate quickly.

Next step: can you confirm which regions and peak qps you expect (EAST-US primary, EU DR?), and whether you're open to a staged availability uplift tied to a dedicated capacity commitment?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0189

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@quantara.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SLA terms for Quantara deployment — uptime and credits

Tim / Karthik — Laura from Legal. I reviewed the commercial proposal and drafted a concise SLA annex to capture the adjustments Karthik proposed. Key commercial/legal points we suggest:

1) Availability commitment: 99.95% monthly for hosted routes. For Dedicated deployments (as defined in the SOW) Redwood will provide a 99.97% monthly uptime commitment for the primary region, provided Quantara maintains the committed capacity for the term.

2) Remedy calculation: Monthly credit tiers tied to the percent below target: 0.45-0.05% below = 10% credit; 0.95-0.46% below = 25% credit; >0.95% below = 50% credit. Credits are applied as a percentage of the affected route's monthly invoice and aggregate monthly credits shall be capped at 40% of monthly fees.

3) Ramp exception: For the first 90 days after go-live, parties agree to a temporary monthly cap of 60% for Quantara, to account for initial stabilization. After day 90, the cap reverts to 40% unless parties agree otherwise in writing.

4) Latency: We are willing to include a p95 latency obligation for designated "user-facing" endpoints (to be listed in an appendix). If the p95 latency target is missed on more than two discrete measurement windows in a 30-day period, Quantara may request a remediation credit up to a single invoice’s 5% (not cumulative with availability credits for the same window). Batched inference endpoints will have separate, relaxed latency thresholds in the appendix.

5) Allocation/proration: Credits will be prorated to the affected routes/services. No uncapped monetary refunds. We cannot accept uncapped monthly credits tied to sustained downtime — it introduces financial exposure that requires an alternative procurement structure (e.g., a dedicated SLA escrow).

6) Measurement & Dispute: Redwood will publish uptime and latency metrics on the Console. Disputes must be raised within 30 days of the metric publication window with supporting logs and timestamps; both parties agree to a 15-day remediation review period before credits are finalized.

Attached is a redline of the SLA annex (Redwood_SLA_Annex_draft.pdf). Karthik / Ben — can you confirm ops can support the proposed p95 measurement windows for user routes and that the 90-day elevated cap is operationally acceptable? Tim — if Quantara can commit to a Dedicated seat or a 12-month committed spend, Legal will fast-track the Annex and we can move to DocuSign.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Annex_draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@quantara.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA terms for Quantara deployment — uptime & monthly credit structure

Karthik / Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Quantara is prepared to move forward on the following compromise:

- Availability: Accept 99.95% for hosted endpoints, with a path to 99.97% once Dedicated capacity is provisioned (we're comfortable committing to a 12-month dedicated capacity agreement).
- Credits: Accept tiered remedy with a 60% monthly cap for the first 90 days, then 40% thereafter. We appreciate the explicit per-incident tiers and the proration language.
- Latency: We'll identify up to three user-facing routes for a p95 annex. We can accept a modest latency credit (single invoice 5%) post the two-strike threshold; batched routes will be listed as tolerant up to p95=400ms in the appendix.

Please send the DocuSign link for the Annex and SOW. Once signed, procurement will trigger the committed capacity purchase and we can schedule a provisioning kick-off.

One small ask: during the initial 90-day ramp, can Redwood provide a biweekly operational sync (30–45 minutes) with Ben/ops to review metrics and any incidents? That will help avoid surprises and accelerate resolution.

If you can add the DocuSign link and schedule the first sync, we’ll route internally and push the SOW sign.

Best,
Tim
Head of Infrastructure, Quantara
procurement@quantara.io

Related: DocuSign prep link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare?doc=QNT-SLA-ANNEX-2027
